title: Pizza de molde en la avenida Corrientes

dialogue.speaker: Lucas
dialogue.spanish: Che, Agus, ¡qué buena estuvo la obra de teatro! Pero ahora tengo un hambre bárbaro.
dialogue.english: Hey, Agus, that play was so good! But now I'm super hungry.

dialogue.speaker: Agustina
dialogue.spanish: Mal, yo también estoy muerta de hambre. Mirá, entremos a esta pizzería clásica acá en Corrientes.
dialogue.english: Totally, I'm starving too. Look, let's go into this classic pizzeria right here on Corrientes Avenue.

slang.actualMeaning: Totally! / Tell me about it! / I agree 100%! (Argentine slang affirmation)
slang.example: —Hace muchísimo calor hoy. —¡Mal, no se aguanta!

dialogue.speaker: Lucas
dialogue.spanish: Bueno, el salón del fondo está lleno, pero podemos comer de parado en la barra como hace todo el mundo.
dialogue.english: Well, the back dining room is full, but we can eat standing up at the counter like everyone else does.

dialogue.speaker: Agustina
dialogue.spanish: ¡Re va! Pidamos dos porciones de muzzarella bien gratinada y dos de fugazzeta rellena con fainá.
dialogue.english: I'm totally down! Let's order two slices of melted mozzarella pizza and two of stuffed onion fugazzeta with chickpea flatbread.

slang.actualMeaning: That totally works! / I'm totally down for that!

dialogue.speaker: Lucas
dialogue.spanish: O sea, con eso quedamos pipón. Yo pido en la caja y traigo dos aguas con gas bien frías.
dialogue.english: I mean, with that we'll be stuffed. I'll order at the register and bring two ice-cold sparkling waters.

dialogue.speaker: Agustina
dialogue.spanish: Dale, genial, yo voy guardando este rincón de la barra antes de que salga la gente del otro teatro.
dialogue.english: Awesome, I'll hold this corner of the counter before the crowd from the other theater gets out.

questions.question: Where did Lucas and Agustina just come from before stopping at the pizzeria?
options: A theater play ('la obra de teatro') on Corrientes Avenue
A soccer game at the stadium
A late shift at the hospital
questions.explanation: Lucas says: '¡qué buena estuvo la obra de teatro! Pero ahora tengo un hambre bárbaro.'

questions.question: Why do they decide to eat standing up at the counter ('de parado en la barra')?
options: The back dining room is full, and eating at the counter is a classic tradition there
The pizzeria is closing in five minutes
They are waiting for a takeaway box
questions.explanation: Lucas notes: 'el salón del fondo está lleno, pero podemos comer de parado en la barra como hace todo el mundo.'

questions.question: What specific food order does Agustina suggest?
options: Two slices of mozzarella and two slices of stuffed onion fugazzeta with fainá
One large pepperoni pizza and a salad
Four beef empanadas and red wine
questions.explanation: Agustina says: 'Pidamos dos porciones de muzzarella bien gratinada y dos de fugazzeta rellena con fainá.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: When Agustina replies '¡Mal!' and '¡Re va!', what do those Argentine expressions mean in context?
options: '¡Mal!' = Totally / I completely agree!; '¡Re va!' = I'm totally down / That works great!
'¡Mal!' = I feel sick; '¡Re va!' = Leave right now!
'¡Mal!' = That's wrong; '¡Re va!' = It's too expensive
'¡Mal!' = Bad service; '¡Re va!' = The bus is coming
questions.explanation: In Argentine slang, replying '¡Mal!' to a friend's statement means 'Totally / Tell me about it!', and '¡Re va!' means 'That totally works / I'm in!'
